title: Medic for Apache Spark - First Aid for Failing Jobs - Drasko Profirovic, Pinterest
talk_summary: Pinterest built an agentic Spark diagnostics tool and iterated from a single ReAct agent with one mega-prompt to a multi-agent architecture with specialized prompts, MCP tools, and a record/playback eval harness. Key wins came from observability (OpenTelemetry→LangFuse), fixture-based offline evals, and pre-processing noisy inputs (log exception clustering, metrics-as-images) in sub-agents to protect the parent context window.

takeaways.technique: Record/playback fixture harness with offline evals
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the agent against real downstream systems in record mode, save tool responses as checked-in fixtures, then replay offline and grade the output report against codified expectations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: In record mode, the agent calls real downstream systems, and tool responses are captured as fixtures... Playback mode, the agent runs against fixtures instead of production data

takeaways.technique: Pre-process noisy inputs in sub-agents, return summaries
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of feeding raw logs/metrics to the main agent, a quarantine sub-agent clusters/filters exceptions and converts time series to annotated images, returning only a summary to the parent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Our sub agent would summarize its findings and return the results back to the parent agent, thereby ensuring the context window is kept healthy.

takeaways.what_they_do: Learn which exceptions appear in successful jobs, treat those as red herrings, cluster and rank remaining exceptions by relevance and recency before showing the agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we would learn which exceptions commonly appear in successful jobs, treat those as likely red herrings, and filter them out

takeaways.technique: Specialized prompts + tool subsets per agent, parallel hypothesis research
takeaways.what_they_do: Split one mega-prompt into role-specific agents each with a dedicated prompt and subset of MCP tools; a supervisor fans out failure hypotheses to parallel research agents, scores them, and picks the highest-confidence root cause.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic workflows are brittle; prefer ReAct
takeaways.what_they_do: They tried LangGraph deterministic workflows but found them brittle versus the reasoning-and-acting paradigm, and kept ReAct with guardrail tools (to-do list, virtual FS).
takeaways.evidence_quote: We trialed using LangGraph's workflows to make the agent more deterministic, but this approach proved to be brittle compared to the reasoning and acting agent paradigm.

takeaways.technique: Trace waterfall observability for agent runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Publish OpenTelemetry traces to LangFuse and view agent execution as a waterfall of steps to diagnose why quality dropped.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We used open telemetry to publish traces to LangFuse. And by viewing the agent's execution as a waterfall diagram of steps, we could better understand the cause of lower quality responses.
